front.title: A Closed-Profile Ruling on Cryptographic Algorithm Inventories for the CNSA 2.0 Acquisition Gate

abstract.t: National security systems of the United States are moving to the algorithms of the Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0, on a published NSA timeline. An acquiring party receives from each supplier an inventory of the cryptographic algorithms its product carries, in a supplier-chosen spelling, and has no shared procedure for ruling on that inventory. This document specifies a closed profile of the CNSA 2.0 algorithm set, a name-folding step, a ruling procedure that returns one verdict and one reason for every entry, a pair of digests over the canonical input and the canonical ruling, and conformance vectors. The ruling is a pure function of published tables, so any two parties who hold the same tables and the same inventory reach the same digests. A keyed mode lets two parties compare digests while keeping the inventory from everyone else. A ruling is a verdict against a published profile and carries the endorsement of no agency.
